findings.title: queue_pool is created once per factory but destroyed on strategy close, breaking processing after a rebalance
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool` is constructed once in `__init__` and reused by every `create_with_partitions` call. `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()`/`terminate()` calls `self.queue_pool.shutdown()`, which permanently stops the worker threads and shuts down the queues. Arroyo calls `create_with_partitions` again after every partition revoke/assign (rebalance), so the second strategy will be handed a pool whose workers are dead and whose queues raise `ShutDown` on put. From then on the consumer silently accepts messages that are never processed and never commits, i.e. it stalls permanently until the process is restarted. The pool needs to be created per strategy (or recreated when it has been shut down).

findings.title: Arroyo commit callback invoked from a background thread
findings.body: `_commit_loop` runs in its own thread and calls `self.commit_function(...)` (ultimately arroyo's `commit` passed to `create_with_partitions`). Arroyo's commit callback and the underlying Kafka consumer are not thread-safe and are expected to be called from the strategy/processing thread (the same thread that calls `poll`/`submit`). Calling it concurrently with the StreamProcessor's own consumer operations can corrupt consumer state or crash librdkafka. Offsets should instead be accumulated and committed from `poll()`.

findings.title: No final commit on close(), and offset state survives rebalances
findings.body: `close()` sets `shutdown_event` (ending `_commit_loop` without a last pass) and then shuts the pool down after workers drain remaining queued items. Offsets for everything processed since the last 1-second tick, plus everything drained during shutdown, are therefore never committed, so those messages are reprocessed after restart. Additionally `OffsetTracker` state (`all_offsets`, `outstanding`, `last_committed`) is never reset on partition revocation; because the pool/tracker is shared across `create_with_partitions` calls, a new strategy can commit offsets for partitions the consumer no longer owns. A final `get_committable_offsets()`/commit after draining, plus per-assignment tracker reset, is needed.

findings.title: Unbounded queues provide no backpressure despite docstring claim
findings.body: `queue.Queue()` is created with no maxsize and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` never raises `MessageRejected`. The class docstring claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", but in practice a slow group can accumulate unbounded work items (each holding the decoded result and the original Kafka `Message`), growing memory without limit and making the uncommitted offset window unbounded. Set a maxsize and raise `MessageRejected` when full so arroyo throttles consumption.

findings.title: Decode/submit failures are silently acked instead of DLQ'd
findings.body: In `submit`, any exception (including the `assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)` and the `assert not isinstance(payload, FilteredPayload)` inside `decode_payload`) is swallowed and the offset is immediately marked added+complete, so the message is committed as if processed. This drops messages without routing them to the DLQ and will also silently discard every `FilteredPayload` while logging an exception for each. Filtered payloads should be handled explicitly and genuine failures should be surfaced/DLQ'd rather than acked.

findings.title: queue.ShutDown / Queue.shutdown require Python 3.13
findings.body: `queue.ShutDown` and `Queue.shutdown(immediate=...)` were added in Python 3.13. On an older interpreter the module-level reference raises `AttributeError` at worker runtime and `q.shutdown()` is swallowed by the broad `except Exception` in `FixedQueuePool.shutdown`, leaving workers blocked forever in `work_queue.get()` and making shutdown hang for 5s per worker. If the project must support <3.13, use a sentinel item to stop workers instead.

findings.title: Transaction name hardcodes "monitors" prefix for generic remote-subscription consumer
findings.body: The sentry_sdk transaction is named `f"monitors.{self.identifier}.worker_{self.worker_id}"`, but this strategy is generic to remote subscriptions (uptime being the first user). Uptime traffic will be reported under a `monitors.*` transaction name, making performance data misleading.
